title: Director of Advanced Manufacturing Engineering
text:
**Position Title:**
Director of Advanced Manufacturing Engineering

**Location:**
Milwaukee, WI

**Position Summary:**

*Join a rapidly growing and market leading manufacturer as the Director of Advanced Manufacturing Engineering. Under the direction of and reporting to the VP of Manufacturing, the Director of Advanced Manufacturing Engineering leads the Manufacturing Engineering function and is accountable for five connected processes:*

* *Standard documentation and engineering change order (ECO) execution*
* *Manufacturing process and technology development in support of New Product Development (NPD), ensuring new products are designed for scalable, repeatable manufacturing*
* *Core technology capital equipment life cycle strategy, including the multi-year roadmap for acquiring, standardizing, deploying, and retiring manufacturing equipment for forming and finishing*
* *Manufacturing system design (MSD) including layout, line balance, material flow, and cell design*
* *Sustainment engineering in support of the value streams.*

*Core technology and MSD are developed in collaboration with the Director of Continuous Improvement and the Director of Manufacturing, and sustainment priorities are set with the Director of Manufacturing and the value stream leaders. The role leads the Manufacturing Team and partners with Design Engineering, Quality, Supply Chain, Finance, and Maintenance/Continuous Improvement.*

**Responsibilities:**

Engineering Change Order (ECO) Execution & Engineering Process Standards

* Own execution of the engineering change order (ECO) process end to end — intake, cross-functional impact review, approval routing, and implementation and cutover tracking — across fabrication and assembly, delivered through the Manager, NPD & Standard Documentation and the ECO resources reporting to that manager.
* Define and maintain manufacturing engineering process standards (BOM, routing, and work-instruction data integrity; drawing and specification standards; standard work definitions) and ensure they are consistently applied across value streams.
* Partner with Value Stream/Area Managers on the floor to ensure engineering standards are followed and gaps are closed, including standard-work sustainment audits, with sustaining engineers providing technical support through the Sustainment Lead.
* Participate in engineering design reviews; evaluate and approve standards for drawings, routings, specifications, and other manufacturing engineering documents.
* Provide the engineering-standards backbone that CI initiatives draw on when Value Stream/Area Managers and sustaining engineers pursue process improvements.

New Product Manufacturing Process Development

* Serve as the manufacturing engineering technology lead within the SOP-2 stage-gate process for new product programs, with primary focus on Phases P0–P2 (Business Case, Concept Design, Design Verification) — evaluating process technology options, make/buy decisions, and automation feasibility ahead of Beta Build — delivered through the Manager, NPD and the NPD engineers.
* Partner with Design Engineering during concept and design verification to ensure new products are designed for manufacturability (DFM/DFA), influencing product design before it is locked.
* Lead process and technology piloting, proof-of-concept builds, and equipment trials for new products, validating manufacturing feasibility and supporting Beta Build (P3), Production Readiness (P4), launch, and ramp to rate; hand off to sustainment engineering and the Value Stream/Area Manager for ownership after launch.
* Own the manufacturing readiness input to the P2 CapEx approval gate — defining the equipment, tooling, and automation investment required to support each new product launch, and building the business case with Finance.
* Represent Advanced Manufacturing Engineering at QRB/PRB stage-gate reviews, ensuring manufacturing technology risk is surfaced and mitigated early in the program.

Capital Equipment Life Cycle Planning

* Develop and maintain a multi-year capital equipment roadmap for forming and finishing across fabrication and assembly, aligned to the product roadmap, capacity plan, and overall plant strategy, in collaboration with the Director of Continuous Improvement and the Director of Manufacturing.
* Own the technical scope and justification for Capital Authorization Requests (CARs), partnering with Finance and plant leadership on prioritization, ROI, and total cost of ownership.
* Define an equipment standardization strategy to reduce total cost of ownership, spare-parts complexity, and technician training burden across the equipment fleet.
* Plan equipment replacement, upgrade, and end-of-life timing using Operational Availability (OA) trends, maintenance cost history, and technology obsolescence risk.
* Partner with Maintenance and Continuous Improvement on the Capital Equipment OA dashboards to identify chronically underperforming assets and translate the trend data into replacement, rebuild, or upgrade decisions.
* Direct capital project execution — technology selection, specification, supplier management, factory and site acceptance testing (FAT/SAT), installation, and equipment support for lasers, presses, and controls — through the Manager, Core Technology and the forming/finishing engineers, controls engineer, and capital equipment technicians.
* Manage the Manufacturing Engineering department budget, including advanced engineering and capital planning activities and tracking actual capital spend against the annual operating plan (AOP) capital budget; support post-installation return reviews on major capital projects.

Manufacturing System Design (MSD)

* Own factory flow design — layout, line balance, material flow, and cell design — and the standard design methodology used across the value streams, developed in collaboration with the Director of Continuous Improvement and the Director of Manufacturing.
* Assign MSD leadership to a designated senior forming/finishing engineer under the Manager, Core Technology, and review whether dedicated MSD headcount is warranted once the workload is visible.
* Drive adoption of MSD design standards and measure results in throughput and space and labor productivity.

Sustainment Engineering (Value Stream Support)

* Own sustainment engineering for the three value streams — process stability, yield, scrap, cost-down, problem solving, and repeat-issue closure —sustaining engineers, with a dotted-line relationship to each value stream leader.
* Set sustainment priorities with the Director of Manufacturing and the value stream leaders, and decide the allocation of engineering capacity between project work and reactive support so that project time is protected.

Advanced Manufacturing Technology & Automation

* Evaluate and recommend automation, robotics, and advanced fabrication/joining technology (e.g., laser welding, automated assembly cells) to advance Company’s manufacturing capability.
* Build technology pilots and investment business cases for automation projects, then partner with the responsible Value Stream/Area Manager on implementation and sustaining support once deployed.
* Benchmark Company’s manufacturing technology against industry best practice and maintain awareness of emerging capital equipment technology relevant to the company's product lines.

Cross-Functional Leadership & Governance

* Lead, coach, and develop the Manufacturing Engineering team providing project management leadership through those leaders and cross-functional project teams; build succession depth for each process.
* Own a single process model across the five processes and its handoff chain — NPD, then MSD, then core technology (installation), then sustainment after launch — with ECO supporting all four; publish decision rights and the handoff model with the VP of Manufacturing, the Director of Manufacturing, and the Director of Continuous Improvement.
* Partner with Product Development, Quality, Supply Chain, Operations, and Finance on stage-gate reviews, launches, prioritization, and risk reviews, and represent manufacturing in design decisions (DFM/DFA) and cost targets.
* Support ISO 9001 and ISO 13485 requirements for new equipment qualification and process validation (PPAP, PFMEA, Control Plans) on new capital assets and ECOs.
* Follow company manufacturing best practices — Standard Work, Visual Factory, and 5S — when deploying new processes, equipment, and engineering changes.

**Key Performance Measures:**

* ECO cycle time (submission to implementation) and engineering process standards compliance across value streams.
* On-time delivery of manufacturing readiness milestones at each NPD stage gate (P0–P3).
* Operational Availability (OA) trend for newly deployed and recently replaced capital assets.
* Capital plan adherence — actual spend vs. AOP capital budget, and realized ROI on major capital projects.
* Reduction in unplanned downtime and total cost of ownership across the managed equipment portfolio.
* Sustainment results across the value streams - first-pass yield, scrap, cost-down delivered, and repeat issue closure.
* Throughput and space and labor productivity gains from manufacturing system design projects.
* Team health - retention, succession coverage, and engagement.
* Number of automation/technology pilots successfully converted to full production deployment.

**Required Qualifications:**

* Bachelor's degree in Mechanical, Manufacturing, or Industrial Engineering (or related field); 12+ years in manufacturing/process engineering, including 5+ years leading engineering teams with budget responsibility, and demonstrated leadership of capital equipment, automation, and engineering change management.
* Proven experience leading new product introduction from a manufacturing engineering perspective — DFM/DFA, process validation, PPAP — within a stage-gate NPD process.
* Direct experience owning an engineering change order (ECO) process and manufacturing engineering data/process standards (BOM, routing, work instructions).
* Strong background evaluating, specifying, and financially justifying capital equipment investment and managing a capital portfolio (business cases, ROI, total cost of ownership, Operational Availability).
* Familiarity with automation and robotics technology in fabrication or assembly environments; experience with laser cutting, forming, and welding automation a plus.
* Lean manufacturing / continuous improvement experience in a low-volume, high-mix manufacturing environment.
* Working knowledge of manufacturing system design, layout, line balance, cell design, and standard work.
